issue.title: fix(mcp): use request-derived base URL for OAuth login redirect and well-known discovery

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
## Description

Fixes #6628 — MCP OAuth flows were unusable behind a reverse proxy.

### Problem 1: Login redirect used the internal container origin

The `/api/mcp/oauth/authorize` route redirect to `/auth/login` was built from `url.origin`, which resolves to the internal container hostname (`<container-id>:3000`) when Homarr runs in Docker behind a proxy.

MCP OAuth URLs now use the configured public `BASE_URL` when present. Deployments without `BASE_URL` retain the existing `x-forwarded-proto` / `x-forwarded-host` / `host` fallback.

### Problem 2: `/.well-known/oauth-*` discovery endpoints returned 404

Next.js's App Router does not route folders with a dot prefix, so the OAuth authorization-server and protected-resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` were unreachable. The folders were moved to `well-known/` and rewrites keep the public URLs working:

- `/.well-known/:path*` for RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 root and path-inserted discovery
- `/api/mcp/:transport/.well-known/:path*` for clients using endpoint-appended discovery

Both forms preserve the transport-specific resource or issuer identifier. The MCP `WWW-Authenticate` challenge advertises the matching RFC 9728 path-inserted metadata URL.

No new environment variable or public URL was added. The existing `BASE_URL` behavior is now documented explicitly for OAuth metadata and redirects.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused OAuth metadata tests pass
- [x] Next.js lint passes with no errors
- [x] Next.js typecheck passes
- [x] Docs lint passes with no errors
- [x] No new dependencies

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Added OAuth metadata discovery through standardized `.well-known` endpoints.
  * Added CORS support for metadata requests, including preflight handling.
  * Improved MCP authentication responses with accurate resource paths and host information.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected authentication redirects when using configured or forwarded host details.
  * Added clear errors for unsupported discovery paths.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that `BASE_URL` must be an HTTP(S) origin without paths, credentials, queries, or fragments.
  * Updated proxy configuration examples to include the URL scheme.

body:
Fixed in #6631. Two root causes:

1. **Login redirect used the internal container origin** — `/api/mcp/oauth/authorize` built the redirect to `/auth/login` from `url.origin`, which is `<container-id>:3000` inside Docker. It now derives the base URL from the request headers (`x-forwarded-proto`/`x-forwarded-host`, falling back to `host`) — the same mechanism the rest of Homarr's auth and the OIDC flow use behind a reverse proxy.

2. **`/.well-known/oauth-*` returned 404** — Next.js's App Router doesn't route dot-prefixed folders, so the OAuth discovery endpoints never existed at the public URLs. They're now served via rewrites at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, and the RFC 8414 path-prefixed location under `/api/mcp/:transport/…` (what Cloudflare Access MCP Server Portal requests).

No env vars or public URLs changed, so no configuration changes are required. Once the CI image is green, redeploying should unblock OAuth-based MCP clients (Claude, portal-managed OAuth, etc.).
Can you try the `ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr-test:pr-6631` docker image and let me know if it fixes your issue @SoloStarship ? The message above was an LLM yapping, sorry about that.

The spec constraint that makes this more than a cosmetic bug: RFC 8414 §3.3, which the MCP spec (2026-07-28, Authorization Server Discovery) adopts as a MUST, requires the `issuer` in the metadata document to be identical to the URL the client fetched it from, and a client MUST NOT use the document otherwise. Any issuer or redirect built from the incoming `Host` header breaks as soon as a reverse proxy is in front, which is every Homarr deployment described here. The fix pattern other projects landed this week is to derive every OAuth URL from a single configured public base URL (`BASE_URL` here) and never from the request. From outside, a scan of a deployment behind a proxy shows it as an issuer mismatch, which is the same failure PagerDuty's hosted MCP server has today (pagerduty-mcp-server#169), so it is not a self-hosting-only problem.

issue.title: [Roadmap M5] Build an OAuth protected-resource compatibility harness

labels.name: go

repository.name: dense-mem
repository.description: Self-hosted AI agent memory server with MCP, evidence provenance, typed claims, conflict detection, embeddings, recall, PostgreSQL, and pgvector

issue.body:
## What

Build an executable compatibility harness for Microsoft Entra, PingOne, and generic OIDC/JWT protected-resource deployments, and freeze the configuration/validation contract before enabling OAuth on `/mcp`.

## Why

Enterprise IdPs differ in audience, scope, group/team claim, JWKS rotation, discovery, and client pre-registration behavior. Dense-Mem must validate these differences without becoming an authorization server or storing refresh tokens.

## Current → target

| Current | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Browser SSO and API-key MCP auth | Executable OAuth protected-resource compatibility evidence |
| No MCP resource metadata contract | RFC 9728 metadata/challenge fixtures and provider config schema |
| Production OAuth disabled | Remains disabled in this ticket |

## Dependencies

- #207
- #209

Start only after all dependencies are merged into current `origin/main`. Fetch upstream and create `issue/<number>-<slug>` from that exact tip; do not stack branches.

## Public contract and invariants

- Dense-Mem is a protected resource; customer IdP owns login, MFA, authorization, refresh, and client registration.
- First target is JWT/JWKS; opaque introspection is deferred.
- Provider config freezes issuer, allowed audiences, discovery/JWKS, algorithm allowlist, external-to-internal scope mapping, and optional team-claim name.
- Validate `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, `exp`, `nbf`, signature/key rotation, scopes, and optional team claim.
- No access or refresh token is stored, logged, forwarded, or returned.
- Test RFC 9728 metadata and standards-compliant `WWW-Authenticate` challenges without enabling production routes.

## Implementation boundaries

Extend existing OIDC test infrastructure where possible. Use local signed-JWT/JWKS fixtures for deterministic cases and documented live compatibility probes for Entra/PingOne. Keep harness/provider config isolated from production MCP middleware until M6.

## Wiki impact

Update a matching wiki branch based on current `origin/master`:

- **Request Lifecycle And Security — target protected-resource boundary**
- **User Portal SSO — distinction between browser SSO and MCP OAuth**
- **Configuration — proposed provider fields and secrets boundary**
- **Development And Testing** — register the new E2E scenario, command, fixtures, and release gate.

Draft architecture wording before implementation and mark current-runtime wording only after verification. Keep the issue open until code, wiki, and post-merge evidence agree.

## E2E scenario: `oauth_provider_compatibility`

Run local TLS OIDC/JWKS providers representing Entra, PingOne, and generic OIDC. Exercise discovery, static JWKS, key rotation, multiple audiences, scope mapping, missing/duplicate claims, clock bounds, algorithm confusion, malformed JWT, optional team claim, and RFC 9728 metadata/challenges. Add sanitized live-provider result procedure without committing credentials.

Run the built artifact through real public boundaries with real PostgreSQL/pgvector and Redis where applicable. Isolation-sensitive cases use A/B/C actors. Outbound provider/IdP stubs may isolate only their network boundary; Dense-Mem validation and policy remain real.

## Validation

- JWT/JWKS and RFC fixture tests
- TLS/discovery/key-rotation integration tests
- Configuration closed-schema and redaction tests
- Dependency/vulnerability review
- `./scripts/ci-check.sh`.
- `oauth_provider_compatibility` on the branch and exact merged `main` SHA.
- Full Compose E2E regression.
- Final code/wiki diff inspection.

No retrieval evaluation is required because production authentication remains unchanged.

## Release and rollback

The harness/config schema can ship dormant. Production `/mcp` remains API-key-only. Rollback removes non-runtime fixtures and config types without data impact.

The issue must leave `main` independently releasable. Incomplete later behavior remains dormant and absent from public discovery. Use `Part of #<issue>`; close after wiki publication and post-merge validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three provider profiles have executable fixtures
- [ ] Validation contract is closed and documented
- [ ] Key rotation and algorithm-confusion cases pass
- [ ] No token material crosses persistence/logging boundaries
- [ ] Production MCP auth remains unchanged
- [ ] Wiki and E2E evidence are complete

## Risk

- **Harness optimism:** local fixtures may miss provider constraints. Mitigation: provider-specific profiles plus sanitized live pre-registration checklist.
- **Token leakage:** test failures may print JWTs. Mitigation: redacting test helpers and prohibited-output assertions.
- **Config ambiguity:** audience/team selection could remain underspecified. Mitigation: freeze exact precedence and mismatch behavior before M6.

## Out of scope

- Enabling OAuth on production routes
- Opaque-token introspection
- Client registration or token refresh
- Changing browser SSO sessions

body: @sameerkhansf are you able to tell me if the fix I've sent fixed the issue for you ?

Not the reporter, so I can't test it live. Read the diff though — `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders` still builds issuer/endpoints/redirect from `x-forwarded-*` / `host`. Fine when the proxy forwards those correctly, wrong issuer the moment it doesn't (tunnel in front of nginx, direct hit on :7575), and Host is client-controlled. Why not `BASE_URL` first, headers only if it's unset?

Thanks @sameerkhansf — I updated #6631 so the configured `BASE_URL` is now preferred for MCP OAuth metadata and redirects. Forwarded headers are only used as a fallback when `BASE_URL` is unset. I also added validation and tests for the public origin.

That's the right fix. Pinning the issuer and redirects to a configured `BASE_URL` keeps RFC 8414 §3.3 satisfied no matter what a proxy in front does with `Host` or `x-forwarded-*`, and the header fallback covers the case where it's unset.

Once #6631 merges I'll stand up a homarr instance behind a reverse proxy and run `npx mcpcomp` against it to confirm the issuer holds end to end. I can also contribute a homarr fixture plus a small CI check that fails the build if the advertised issuer ever comes from a request header, so this can't quietly come back. Want me to open that?

(mcpcomp is the scanner from the earlier comment.)
@sameerkhansf as I said earlier, there is already a released demo version that you can try it out on. Could you do that ?

Ran it against `https://demo.homarr.dev/api/mcp/mcp`. Grade C, one requirement violation, and the good news first: the discovery problem from this issue is gone on the demo. The `.well-known` documents serve 200 and the challenge points `resource_metadata` at `https://demo.homarr.dev/...`, the public domain, not an internal container origin. So the BASE_URL fix is doing its job here.

The one graded finding is a different, smaller one on the token-expiry path:

The 401 for a *rejected* token carries no `WWW-Authenticate` header. The no-credential 401 does carry it, but when a client presents an invalid or expired token, the 401 comes back bare. OAuth 2.1 §5.3.1 wants the challenge on that response too, because a client whose token just expired re-discovers the auth server from it. Without the header it falls back to guessing the well-known URIs, which still work here, so it's medium not critical.

Repro (the demo rate-limits repeated probes with 429, so space these out):

```bash
# no credential: 401 WITH the challenge
curl -sD - -o /dev/null -X POST https://demo.homarr.dev/api/mcp/mcp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' | grep -i www-authenticate

# invalid token: 401 WITHOUT the challenge
curl -sD - -o /dev/null -X POST https://demo.homarr.dev/api/mcp/mcp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' | grep -i www-authenticate
```

Fix is to send the same `WWW-Authenticate` header on the rejected-token 401 that the credential-less one already emits.

Two advisories that don't affect the grade, if you're tidying up: the AS advertises a `registration_endpoint` but no Client ID Metadata Documents (DCR is deprecated as of 2026-07-28), and `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` (RFC 9207) isn't advertised.

Happy to send the full report. And the offer still stands to add a homarr fixture plus a CI check so the discovery regression this issue was about can't come back silently.

Pre-fix, this chain broke immediately at the first redirect to an unreachable `<container-id>:3000` address. Confirms the first bug (login redirect using internal origin instead of `BASE_URL`) is fixed.

issue.body:
## What

- serve MCP OAuth discovery through routable `/.well-known` rewrites
- use an optional validated `BASE_URL` public origin for metadata and login redirects behind proxies
- advertise path-specific protected-resource metadata on every MCP 401 response
- preserve canonical `/api/mcp` and compatibility `/api/mcp/mcp` resources
- document `BASE_URL` and correct the proxy example scheme

This is a focused v2 port of the relevant work from #6631, with the invalid/expired-token challenge feedback addressed. It avoids that PR's unrelated stale `dev` changes.

Closes #6628.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run 'apps/nextjs/src/app/api/mcp/[transport]/route.spec.ts'` (16 passed)
- `pnpm turbo typecheck --filter=@homarr/nextjs`
- `pnpm turbo build --filter=@homarr/docs`
- production `@homarr/nextjs` Turbopack build
- production-server smoke of root/path-inserted authorization and resource metadata, canonical and compatibility MCP routes, and missing/malformed/rejected credential challenges using `BASE_URL=https://homarr.example.com`
- valid `BASE_URL` origin import succeeds; a URL containing a path is rejected
